_comment: PLAT-37 / PLAT-35 — THE FIRST GPUI-vs-ELECTRON PARITY READING TAKEN IN ONE
CAPTURE SESSION. **NOT against one build — see `provenance.buildSkew`.**
THE HEADLINE THIS FILE FIRST CARRIED WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE
MOST IMPORTANT THING IN IT. `Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md` 2.2 rule 4
requires a tier-4 review to be 'against the same build'. The earlier passes
failed that because the Electron set was captured 2026-10-02 and the GPUI
set 2026-10-07 — two capture DATES. This pass fixed the capture dates (both
sets are within 11 minutes of each other on 2026-10-12, one checkout, one
recording, one engine named through REPLAY_SERVER_BIN) and then claimed rule
4 was satisfied. It is not. Aligning WHEN THE PIXELS WERE TAKEN is not the
same as aligning WHAT WAS RUNNING, and the review that caught this found the
GPUI arm running a binary 127 commits behind the Electron arm.
So the rule-4 defect was not removed, it was MOVED ONE LEVEL DOWN: from the
capture date to the build date, where nothing was looking. Every GPUI-side
finding below is therefore a reading of codetracer as it stood on
2026-10-07, compared against Electron as it stood on 2026-10-12. Findings
are tagged `buildSkewContaminated` accordingly, and one (PARITY-S2) is
withdrawn outright because the skew fully explains it.
THIS FILE IS NOT A GATE AND IS NOT THE TIER-4 LEDGER. It records what was
measured. `src/tests/visual/tier4-gpui-readings.json` is PLAT-35's and
carries its own integrity suite; nothing here was written to it. NOTHING
GATES THIS FILE EITHER — see `provenance.buildSkew.whatWouldHaveCaughtIt`.
GEOMETRY FIRST, PIXELS SECOND. Three of the six scenarios are at the
`wide` viewport, where Electron honours 1920x1080 exactly and GPUI is
clamped by AppKit to 1728x1084. Those three have NO pixel comparison at
all — not a lenient one, none — because comparing two different extents
is a number about resampling rather than about the product. They are
still compared STRUCTURALLY, which needs no common extent.
WHAT EACH NUMBER CAME FROM, so no reader has to guess which instrument
made a claim:
* `stoppedLine.gpui`      — the PLAT-39 screen oracle's readGutterDigits
over the GPUI window capture (Apple Vision OCR).
* `stoppedLine.electron`  — the SAME oracle over the Electron capture.
`null` means the oracle REFUSED the frame
(grammar-mismatch), not that the line is absent;
`electronRouteLine` carries the product's own
answer for the same frame.
* `electronRouteLine`     — window.data.services.debugger.location, read by
the lane's Playwright driver after each operation.
NOT OCR, so it is an independent instrument.
* `flip`                  — NVIDIA FLIP via codetracer-image-diff's flip(),
over ffmpeg-decoded RGBA. No second differ was
written (30/30a); magick/compare are absent here.
* `structural` findings   — read off the point-extent PNGs by disposable
sub-agents, one per frame pair, each capped at
250 words. Locations are POINTS in the content
area and are approximate to a few points.

2026-10-13, RE-REVIEW: three statements in this file are WRONG and are corrected in place by sibling `*Correction` fields that keep the wrong text beside them — provenance.buildSkew.positiveControl (the @lpkTimeline leg), PARITY-S10 (both halves) and PARITY-G1 ("Electron's fit inside their pane"). None of the three is a build-skew casualty: each was wrong about the frames in front of the reader. The `buildSkewContaminated` flags are DELIBERATELY LEFT SET — they are true statements about this pass and are the evidence that the contamination happened. The re-measured, freshness-gated pass is a SEPARATE file, plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-13.json; this one is not updated to describe it, because a dated record rewritten to say something else stops being a record.
standing: HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE — neither lane is a gate; both need a live macOS GUI session and a Screen Recording grant.

provenance.whyUncommittedIsStated: AGENTS.md: say what you measured it against — and a sha alone would have been a lie here. Neither file is in the capture or the replay path: the first governs how the dev shell builds .python-recorder-venv, the second how the TUI fixture provider decides to re-record. Both bear on how the RECORDING was produced, not on how either lane reads it.

engine.why: the CARGO target, which is what findReplayServer reaches; src/build-debug-repro/bin is not in its candidate list at all. Exported as REPLAY_SERVER_BIN to BOTH lanes so the choice is recorded rather than inherited.

gpuiBinary.why: the binary `ci/test/plat37-macos-window-capture.sh` runs. The lane sets BIN=${root}/build/bin/codetracer-gpui and only checks `[ -x ]` (line 187); it never builds it and never compares it against HEAD.
gpuiBinary.note: THIS IS THE GPUI ARM'S ACTUAL EXECUTABLE AND IT WAS MISSING FROM THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE, which recorded only the Rust shim. A provenance table that omits the binary under test cannot show a build skew, which is why this one did not.

measuredHow: The Timeline panel was removed by `740d76be2`, 2026-10-08T02:19:56 +0300 — 8.5 hours AFTER the GPUI binary was built.
Four of the 127 touch the GPUI window/host code itself: 740d76be2, 1fdcc0c5c (welcome tab, focus highlight, drop zones, LIVE RESIZE), 5dea7f072 and ac6e304a5 (keymaps).
buildSkew.positiveControl: the stale binary still carries symbols the current tree does not: `grep -a` finds `@Timeline` (a pane-name-table entry beside `@Flow`), `@lpkTimeline` (a PaneKind spelling that no longer exists) and the mangled Nim symbol `_renderTimeline__appZleaves_` — a proc in `gpui/app/leaves.nim`, a file that at 8f284d063 contains no `Timeline` at all. Negative control: the nonsense literal `ZZZ_no_such_literal_ZZZ` -> 0. At 8f284d063, `PaneKind` has no `paneTimeline`, `RetiredPaneSpellings == ["timeline"]`, `shared_default_layout.generated.json` contains the string zero times, and `test_shared_default_layout.nim`'s `paneTimelineIsGone()` asserts it.
buildSkew.consequence: Every GPUI-side finding describes codetracer at 2026-10-07, not at 8f284d063. The Electron-side and instrument findings (PARITY-S8, PARITY-S12, PARITY-I1, PARITY-O1) are unaffected: that arm was built the same day it was captured.
buildSkew.whatWouldHaveCaughtIt: Nothing in the tree compares the GPUI binary's mtime against the newest commit touching `src/frontend/gpui/` or `src/frontend/headless_app/`. The capture lane's `[ -x ${BIN} ]` is an EXISTENCE check, which is the same defect shape as `issues/2026-10-07-gpui-plan-lane-runs-against-an-unchecked-replay-server-and-blames-the-product.md` records for `replay-server` — a different binary and a different lane, same family. Filed as its own issue; see `reviewFindings`.
buildSkew.whyRule4DidNotCatchIt: `Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md` §2.2 rule 4 DOES exist and IS enforced — but on `tier4-review.json`, and it binds the REVIEW's `againstUiBundleMtime` to the CAPTURE's provenance. It therefore asks 'did the reviewer look at the build that was photographed', not 'was the build that was photographed the one we are drawing conclusions about'. Both would have read 2026-10-07 here and rule 4 would have passed. The unasserted edge is capture-build against SOURCE.
buildSkew.positiveControlCorrection: CORRECTED ON RE-REVIEW 2026-10-13, against codetracer df80efc8d with a REBUILT and FRESHNESS-GATED GPUI binary. The wrong text is kept above rather than overwritten: this file is the record of the 2026-10-12 contaminated pass, and an error silently repaired is an error the next reader cannot learn from. The re-measured readings live in plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-13.json. THE `@lpkTimeline` LEG OF THIS CONTROL IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED. It is described above as 'a PaneKind spelling that no longer exists'. It is not a PaneKind spelling at all: it is `LogicalPanelKind.lpkTimeline` in src/frontend/viewmodel/collab/types.nim, the COLLAB panel enum, present at df80efc8d. Measured 2026-10-13 with `grep -ac`: `@lpkTimeline` -> 1 in the REBUILT build/bin/codetracer-gpui and `lpkTimeline` -> 1 in src/build-debug-repro/ui.js. It is present on BOTH sides and in BOTH builds, so it cannot discriminate between them and is not evidence of staleness. The OTHER TWO legs hold and are what the control rests on: `@Timeline` read 2 in the stale binary and reads 0 in the rebuilt one, and `_renderTimeline__appZleaves_` likewise. Gated: positive control `Call Trace` -> 1, negative control `ZZQQnonsense_literal_XYZZY` -> 0.

instrumentControls: GPUI lane controls 1-3 passed: host/grant/display still; a capture aimed at a non-existent owner REFUSED with attestation matched 0 and no G1 claim; the grader's rendersText assertion made to fail on a synthesised flat frame.
The GPUI windowed shim was probed in BOTH polarities for the font-kit literal (font_kit=1, 'no text will be rendered'=0), so the textless-window failure mode is excluded.

FLIP driver controlled before use: identical 64x64 buffers -> mean 0.0 on every statistic; a 16x16 white block in the same frame -> mean 0.0719 with the hot tiles exactly over the block. Both arms live.
Engine symbol probe carries a negative control (a nonsense symbol -> 0), which AGENTS.md's own 320c37ed recipe lacks.

REVIEW, 2026-10-12: the FLIP driver's controls were RE-RUN independently rather than taken on report. Identical 64x64 buffers -> every statistic exactly 0.0. A 16x16 white block injected into one of them -> nonzero with the hot tiles exactly over the block and its spatial-filter spill. A deliberate width/height mismatch -> `flipdiff` exits 3 with 'buffer size mismatch' and computes nothing, so the 'never resample' claim is enforced in code and not merely asserted in a comment. The implementer's specific 0.0719 constant could not be reproduced (the control's own inputs were not retained) and is recorded as unverifiable; the control's PURPOSE — a live, localising positive arm — was reproduced.

REVIEW: `nim check` on the modified `fixture_provider.nim` exits 0, gated on a positive control (an undefined symbol appended to the same file makes it exit 1 and name the symbol); the file was restored by byte copy and its sha256 asserted identical.

The venv interpreter yields `py-f1f2ea4f371abf6a9794cab1`, byte-identical to `provenance.recording.recorderIdentity` — a reproducible positive arm. `/usr/bin/python3` yields exit 1 (ModuleNotFoundError) and therefore the empty identity the asymmetric rule needs, both with and without `-I`.

corpusVerdict.summary: ALL SIX scenarios reach their pinned stop on BOTH front-ends, except entry-shell's Electron ROUTE SAMPLE (see PARITY-I1), whose FRAME is correct. The pins were right and were not moved.
corpusVerdict.stepCountRuling: FIVE stepIns is CORRECT. With an engine carrying 5ba7e8408 the recording opens at tick 1 (<__main__> line 1) rather than tick 0 (the <toplevel> root's synthetic entry), so the five-step trajectory is 1,2,29,34,39,44 and lands on 44. Electron's own location API records entry=1@1 ... stepIn=44@6, and advanced-state's next-chain is 44@6 -> 54@7 -> 55@8 -> 56@9, waypoint for waypoint the chain corpus-pins.json already recorded. The stale engine's trajectory began entry=1@0 and stopped at 39.
corpusVerdict.reviewVerification: VERIFIED ON REVIEW, independently of the GPUI arm and therefore UNAFFECTED by the build skew, because the stopped line is decided by the engine and the corpus and not by the renderer. From the Electron lane's own route artefacts (the product's location API, current build): stepped-editor `entry=1@1 2@2 29@3 34@4 39@5 44@6`, final 44; advanced-state `44@6 next=54@7 55@8 56@9`, final 56, matching corpus-pins' recorded chain `44 -> 54 -> 55 -> 56` waypoint for waypoint; continued-event-log `113@171`; returned-calltrace `stepOut=110@37`. FIVE STEP-INS IS CORRECT and the pins are correct. That the 127-commit-stale GPUI arm reached the same lines is, if anything, a stronger control than a matched build would have been: two renderers of different vintage, two instruments, one engine, same answers.
corpusVerdict.residual: ONE THING THE SETTLEMENT OVERSTATED. 'corpus-pins.json is unchanged and was always right' is true of the PINS and false of their prose. `stepped-editor._why` still opens 'Six step-ins.' and `breakpoint-editor._why` 'Six step-ins, then a gutter mark.' — which is precisely the mismatch the issue was opened about. The rest of that same sentence, 'ticks 1..6 visit lines 1, 2, 29, 34, 39, 44', is exactly right and describes six TICKS reached by five STEPS. So the fix is a two-word prose correction, not a pin change; it is named here rather than made, because corpus-pins.json is PLAT-39's and was not in this pass's scope.

findings.finding: GPUI cannot reach the `wide` viewport on this display, so three of the six scenarios have NO common extent and cannot be pixel-compared at all.
findings.measurement: Electron asked 1920x1080 points and got 1920x1080 (`honouredInCss: true`, deviation {0,0}), captured 3840x2160 device px. GPUI asked the same and got a 1728x1084-point frame (`viewportHonoured: false`, `viewportDeviationPoints` {-192,-25}), captured 3456x2168 device px. After cropping GPUI's 58-device-px title bar the two are 3456x2110 vs 3840x2160 — different in BOTH dimensions.
findings.instrument: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo attestation read by ci/test/plat37_macos_window_capture.nim before any pixel was taken, in both lanes; extents re-read from the PNGs with ffprobe.
findings.consequence: Measured, not inferred: at `wide` the GPUI Call Trace rows are SLICED BY THE WINDOW EDGE at x=1728 — e.g. `evaluate #3(expression="2 + 3") =>` stops mid-text — while Electron's fit inside their pane. The clamp is content loss, not only a smaller picture.
findings.owner: filed as codetracer-specs/issues/2026-10-12-gpui-clamps-a-window-to-the-visible-frame-because-it-never-overrides-constrainframerect-and-electron-does-not.md — AppKit's default constrainFrameRect:toScreen:, which build_window_class never overrides.
findings.buildSkewNote: The GPUI side of this finding was read from a binary built 2026-10-07, 127 commits behind the Electron arm (see provenance.buildSkew). The difference is REAL between the two binaries that were captured; whether it is still real at 8f284d063 is NOT established by this pass and must be re-measured against a rebuilt GPUI.
findings.contentLossVerified: CONFIRMED ON REVIEW by an independent reader, and it is the part of G1 that matters: at `wide` GPUI's Call Trace pane runs from x~1398 to x=1728, the window's right edge, and its rows are cut mid-character by that edge with NO ellipsis — e.g. `evaluate #3(expression="2 + 3") =>`, `apply_op #4(symbol="+", left=2,`, `evaluate #14(expression="100 / 5 -`. Electron's fit inside their pane. This upgrades the clamp from a capture inconvenience to USER-VISIBLE CONTENT LOSS: the user cannot read the call arguments. NOTE the contrast with PARITY-S7, where GPUI elides an over-long STATE value with an ellipsis — so GPUI has the affordance and the Call Trace pane does not use it at this width.
findings.specGrounding: `spec/Testing/Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md` §2.2 rule 3: "a score below 4 blocks … content clipped mid-glyph is content loss. So it is an assertion, not a note." The Call Trace rows at `wide` are clipped mid-glyph by the window edge with no ellipsis, so the spec already classifies this as content loss and as blocking. That settles the question this finding was raised to ask — whether the clamp is merely a smaller picture — against the clamp.
findings.consequenceCorrection: CORRECTED ON RE-REVIEW 2026-10-13, against codetracer df80efc8d with a REBUILT and FRESHNESS-GATED GPUI binary. The wrong text is kept above rather than overwritten: this file is the record of the 2026-10-12 contaminated pass, and an error silently repaired is an error the next reader cannot learn from. The re-measured readings live in plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-13.json. THE CLAUSE "Electron's fit inside their pane" IS FALSE, in both the `consequence` and the `contentLossVerified` fields above. Re-measured 2026-10-13 on the gated `wide` frames by two disposable readers, one per renderer, neither shown the other's answer: ELECTRON CLIPS ITS CALL TRACE ROWS MID-GLYPH TOO, with no ellipsis — e.g. `apply_op #4 (symbol="+", left=2, r`, `evaluate #14 (expression="100 / 5 -`, `apply_op #15 (symbol="/", left=100`. GPUI's rows clip the same way. THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT THE ELLIPSIS, IT IS WHERE AND AGAINST WHAT: Electron clips at a PANE BORDER carrying a vertical scrollbar with the AGENT ACTIVITY panel beyond it, so the content is reachable; GPUI's text runs to the WINDOW EDGE with no border, no scrollbar and nothing beyond, so it is not. The clamp half of G1 therefore STANDS and is the whole of it; the renderer-contrast half does not. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLANNED FIX, and this is why it matters more than its severity: the Step-4 fix queued against this was to give GPUI's `renderCallTrace` the `text-overflow: ellipsis` affordance that `stateCell` has. That fix WAS NOT MADE, deliberately. It would have made GPUI the only renderer that elides a Call Trace row — widening the divergence while closing a parity finding against a green assertion. The source asymmetry is real (`renderCallTrace` sets overflow:hidden and flex-shrink:0 with no `text-overflow` and no `min-width:0`; `stateCell` sets all four) but it is not what this finding measured.
findings.contentLossVerifiedCorrection: SUPERSEDED — see consequenceCorrection. The independent reader who 'CONFIRMED ON REVIEW' this field confirmed the GPUI half, which holds, and carried the Electron half over without re-reading an Electron frame. That is the failure mode this correction exists to name: a re-run that re-captures without re-READING preserves every reading error it inherited.

findings.finding: GPUI's window carries a 29-point macOS title bar that Electron's frameless window does not, so the GPUI frame is 29 points taller than its content for the same request.
findings.measurement: GPUI laptop: windowFramePoints 1440x929, windowContentHeightPoints 1055-... i.e. frame minus content = 29 points = 58 device px at scale 2.0. Cropping exactly 58 device px off the top of all three laptop GPUI frames makes them 2880x1800 — byte-for-byte the extent of the Electron frames.
findings.instrument: the lanes' own capture.json; crop applied with ffmpeg, never a resample.
findings.ruling: This is the ONLY normalisation applied anywhere in this pass. Electron is never cropped: its attested frame equals getContentSize().
findings.buildSkewNote: The GPUI side of this finding was read from a binary built 2026-10-07, 127 commits behind the Electron arm (see provenance.buildSkew). The difference is REAL between the two binaries that were captured; whether it is still real at 8f284d063 is NOT established by this pass and must be re-measured against a rebuilt GPUI.

findings.finding: At the one viewport where the two CAN be compared, roughly 37% of every frame differs perceptibly, and the three scenarios differ from each other by less than 1 point of that — so what dominates the difference is the CHROME AND LAYOUT, not the scenario content.

measurement.note: p50 is ~0.0001 in all three while p90 is ~0.68: the distribution is bimodal — most pixels agree closely, a large minority disagree almost completely. That is the signature of displaced structure, not of a shading or gamma difference.

findings.instrument: NVIDIA FLIP through codetracer-image-diff ee9fb397b (`flip()`, `renderFlipPng()`), over ffmpeg-decoded RGBA at 2880x1800. No second differ was written.
findings.localisation: FLIP's own per-pixel error aggregated over an 8x6 grid. Worst tile in all three is device-px (1080,0,360,300) at 72-74% — the top of the editor/State boundary, where GPUI's editor ends at x=652 points and Electron's State pane begins at x=580. Calmest tiles are 5.6%, all in the lower-left and lower-right background.
findings.buildSkewNote: The GPUI side of this finding was read from a binary built 2026-10-07, 127 commits behind the Electron arm (see provenance.buildSkew). The difference is REAL between the two binaries that were captured; whether it is still real at 8f284d063 is NOT established by this pass and must be re-measured against a rebuilt GPUI.
findings.localisationVerified: RE-DERIVED ON REVIEW from `flip-results.jsonl` rather than taken on report. Ranked by `fracOver0_10` the worst tile is device-px (1080,0,360,300) in ALL THREE scenarios, at 72.08 / 73.05 / 74.03 % — the quoted '72-74%' — and the calmest is 5.56% in all three, in the lower-left and lower-right background. The tile is points x 540-720, y 0-150, which does straddle GPUI's editor/State boundary (652/660) and Electron's (580). NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE READER: ranked by tile MEAN instead, the worst tile is a different one — (2160,300) — so the statistic the ranking uses has to be named or the localisation is not reproducible. It is `fracOver0_10`.
findings.comparabilityVerified: The frames were re-measured directly: the three `laptop` GPUI PNGs are 2880x1858 and crop to exactly 2880x1800, which is the Electron PNGs' extent to the pixel; Electron is never cropped. The three `wide` pairs are 3456x2168 (crop 3456x2110) vs 3840x2160 and were not compared — and could not have been: `flipdiff` exits 3 on any size mismatch, verified by deliberately feeding it one. So the 37% is over genuinely comparable buffers. Both arms were driven by the SAME capture probe — `SCScreenshotManager/SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow:)` over a real on-screen window attested by `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` before any pixel was taken — so the geometry difference is the product's and not the instrument's.
findings.reviewRuling: THE 37% IS REAL AND CORRECTLY COMPUTED, AND IT IS NOT A PARITY FIGURE. Do not track it as one. Three reasons, in order of force: (1) the three scenarios agree to within 0.63 points (36.39-37.02%), so the metric is nearly BLIND to scenario content — it is measuring the chrome, not the product's answers; (2) the bimodality (p50 0.00005-0.00017 against p90 0.67-0.68) says most pixels agree almost exactly while a large minority disagree almost completely, which is displaced structure, not shading; (3) it is dominated by at least TWO independent structural differences, not one global offset — PARITY-S3's 60-80pt column displacement AND PARITY-S1's two extra Electron panes — so it cannot be corrected by a single translation and cannot be attributed to a single cause. Its legitimate uses are as a BASELINE for this pair of builds and as corroboration of S1/S3. It is meaningless across runs whose layout differs, and this run's GPUI arm is 127 commits stale, so the number should not be carried forward at all.

findings.finding: WITHDRAWN ON REVIEW — NOT A PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Originally filed as 'GPUI's bottom strip carries a Timeline tab; Electron's does not', with Electron implied to be the deficient side. The opposite is true of the product, and neither side is deficient: the Timeline panel was REMOVED FROM EVERY FRONT-END by PLAT-51, and the GPUI binary that was captured predates that removal.
findings.measurement: Frame readings stand and were re-confirmed by a second reader: GPUI bottom tabs are `Event Log` / `Timeline` / `Terminal Output` in all four GPUI frames read (both viewports); Electron's are `EVENT LOG` / `TERMINAL OUTPUT` with no Timeline. But at codetracer 8f284d063 the Timeline does not exist: `PaneKind` has no `paneTimeline` (removed by `740d76be2`, 2026-10-08T02:19:56), `RetiredPaneSpellings == ["timeline"]`, `shared_default_layout.generated.json` contains the string zero times, `src/frontend/gpui/**` outside tests contains it zero times, and `test_shared_default_layout.nim`'s `paneTimelineIsGone()` asserts no PaneKind spells it. The captured `build/bin/codetracer-gpui` is dated 2026-10-07T17:51 — 8.5 hours BEFORE that commit — and still carries `@Timeline`, `@lpkTimeline` and `_renderTimeline__appZleaves_`.
findings.instrument: three independent lines, agreeing: binary mtime vs commit date; `grep -a` symbol probe of the binary against the current sources (with a nonsense-literal negative control); and two disposable frame readers.
findings.ruling: INSTRUMENT ARTEFACT of the stale GPUI binary. Electron is CORRECT to have no Timeline tab. There is no PLAT-51 regression: the assertion in `test_shared_default_layout.nim` holds at 8f284d063 and was never contradicted — the frame that appeared to contradict it was drawn by code that predates it. Nothing to fix in either renderer; the thing to fix is the lane that ran a stale binary.

The wrong text is kept above rather than overwritten: this file is the record of the 2026-10-12 contaminated pass, and an error silently repaired is an error the next reader cannot learn from. findings.finding: The breakpoint lands on a DIFFERENT ABSOLUTE SOURCE LINE in the two renderers — GPUI line 32, Electron line 28 — and both are obeying the corpus correctly.
findings.measurement: GPUI: filled pink/red dot at x~328,y~161 on line 32, first drawn row 31. Electron: smaller red dot at x~288,y~95 on line 28, first drawn row 27. scenarios.json's breakpoint-editor sets `line: 1`, which its own prose defines as RELATIVE TO THE FIRST DRAWN ROW. 31+1=32 and 27+1=28, so each renderer resolved the rule correctly and the results disagree because PARITY-S5's row windows disagree. CONFIRMED ON REVIEW by two instruments per side: the GPUI grader's own OCR sample for this frame reads `"31", "\u2022", "32", "33"` — the bullet between gutter 31 and 32 — and a disposable reader independently read the dot on gutter row 32 with first row 31; on the Electron side a disposable reader read the dot on gutter row 28 with first row 27, and the lane's own route records `setBreakpoint@28`.
findings.ruling: CONFIRMED, and it is a SCENARIO-SPELLING DEFECT — not a defect in either renderer. Both drivers resolved the documented rule correctly and disagreed because their row windows disagree.
findings.definitionSource: MEASURED FROM SOURCE, not inferred. `src/tests/visual/scenarios.json`, `breakpoint-editor._why`: "`line` is relative to the first drawn row and is resolved by each driver against the recording's own source, never against a literal." The same file's `_comment` says `setBreakpoint@<row>` "is an offset into the editor's FIRST DRAWN ROW, which after five stepIns is 31" — and 31 is the GPUI window's first drawn row. Electron's is 27. So scenarios.json's own prose silently assumes one renderer, in a file whose first line is 'IT NAMES NO RENDERER'.
findings.whatItInvalidates: NARROWER THAN FIRST STATED, and the narrowing was measured rather than assumed. It does NOT invalidate 'every setBreakpoint@N reading in this campaign's history'. `src/tests/visual/plat40-scenario.json` carries `setBreakpoint@35` -> `breakpointLine: 36` and is SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: its own `_comment` records that it chose a stop where 'the window's first drawn row is line 1' on both front-ends, and that 'the record asserts the two agree rather than trusting this file'. That is exactly the right handling of this hazard. What IS affected is `scenarios.json`'s `breakpoint-editor` itself — a `setBreakpoint` at a stop whose first drawn rows are 31 and 27 — and its prose's bare '31'.
findings.buildSkewNote: The MECHANISM is skew-independent: a renderer-relative line in a renderer-neutral corpus disagrees whenever the row windows disagree, whatever the build. The ABSOLUTE values 32 and 31 are from the 2026-10-07 GPUI binary and may move on a rebuild; 28 and 27 are current.

The code-column-only band landed in `58939dbe1` (2026-09-23, 'one editor row per line, the execution line banded, a readable gutter'), two weeks BEFORE the 2026-10-07 binary, so the captured stale binary already drew what is drawn today. So: GPUI does NOT band the gutter, Electron's marker is NOT the only orange one, and the grey-vs-orange contrast above does not exist. Corroborated from source: `ExecutionRowBand` in src/frontend/gpui/app/leaves.nim is documented as drawn 'across the CODE COLUMN to the editor's right edge and NOT under the line numbers (PLAT-47 B1)', deliberately matching Monaco — i.e. matching Electron — and its token value #404040 is exactly the RGB(64,64,64) the pixel-sampling reader measured on both sides. placementRuling.question: should these 17 (now 18) readings live here, or be merged into PLAT-35's tier-4 ledger?
placementRuling.ruling: KEEP THEM SEPARATE. The separation is right and merging would be a mistake.
why: `tier4-gpui-readings.json` is PLAT-35's GPUI-ONLY ledger and is GATED by its own integrity suite. This file is a CROSS-RENDERER record with a different schema, a different subject and a different standing ('HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE — neither lane is a gate').

Merging would put an ungated, host-conditional record inside a gate, so a reading nobody can reproduce without a macOS GUI session and a Screen Recording grant would start deciding whether a suite is green.

It would also make the tier-4 ledger's cardinality and integrity assertions answer to a second corpus with different members — the same 'corpus that grew to fit its instrument' hazard `ci/test/plat37-window-frame.sh` already states as a rule.
placementRuling.whatGatesThisFile: NOTHING, and that is the live gap. It is a JSON under `src/tests/visual/` that no suite reads. The minimum worth adding — and the check that would have caught this pass's own defect — is a provenance-freshness assertion: fail if `build/bin/codetracer-gpui`'s mtime predates the newest commit touching `src/frontend/gpui/` or `src/frontend/headless_app/`. A schema/cardinality assertion of the kind `scenarios.json` carries would be worth having too, but it is the freshness check that has already paid for itself once. Worth noting that the mechanism already exists one file over: `test_cross_renderer_visual_alignment.nim` refuses `tier4-review.json` four ways, including a build-provenance equality. This file is outside all four, which is the direct consequence of keeping it separate and is the price of that (correct) decision — so the freshness check has to be added here rather than inherited.
